status: authored 2026-10-22 and carved into the LIVE world that day (R9MN, docs/STATE.md; pinned in live_carve); the 2026-10-23 nest rooms (nests, networks[].nest_rooms) are generated and audited offline only, NOT applied, not seen in game
owner_brief: the owner, 2026-10-21: "with no caves people wont be incentivized to mine at all, it would be really nice to have some really really large and long mines every so often in the world" / "i need some to be thousands long or just somehow carve out caves underground, really need that" / "a few hunderd block caves wont be enoughfor 10 people" / "its looking more like 6 now"
design: Abandoned working mines cut into the rock under the hills of the eastern half (x >= 4096; the western half's natural caves are another builder's). Each network has a timbered adit, main haulage drifts with rails, crosscuts and long side drifts on several levels 16 blocks apart joined by stair inclines and ladder shafts, stopes where six players can work at once, and vanilla ore in the exposed walls. The ore is richer on the deeper levels and the farther from the adit. Everything is a hash of `seed` and the network id (tools/mines.py h32), grown on the canonical heightmap (tools/ground.py, rounded) and never on a world.

rules.x_min_why: the western half belongs to the natural-cave builder; stay at least 64 blocks east of x 4096
rules.river_corridor_why: data/water_shape.json rivers.defaults.corridor_half_width_blocks: the audit's footprint for a revised reach, so a meander may sit anywhere in it
rules.y_floor_min_why: the lowest floor, with its 2-block shell under it, stays well above the bedrock

nests.owner_words: "I would also like some random room to be added where we have habitat blocks spawning a nest or something." (2026-10-22)
nests.why: 1 or 2 rooms a network, ADDED to the live 2026-10-22 working (live_carve): from the dead end of a side drift or crosscut a straight drift 3 wide and side_height tall runs spur_len on, then opens into an elliptical cavity the miners broke into, 12 to 20 across, a domed roof `tall` high, with no timber, rail or lantern; the room keeps room_clear from every other carved cell and the spur spur_clear past its first two cells, so it is reached only by its spur; no fitting of the working moves (the generator compares them and fails closed). One activated Habitat Block in the floor under the middle (tools/nest_rooms.py). Sited once by `python tools/mine_networks.py nests --site` into networks[].nest_rooms

live_carve.what: the cells R9MN carved into the live world on 2026-10-22, per network: the count and sha256 of the int32 (x, y, z) triples, sorted by x, then y, then z, of every air write in the pass-1 carve section of the as-installed pack (built from a7ccab43, the code and data of that install). Pillar columns are counted: the pack carves them, then the fittings stand the pillars in them
live_carve.rule: the generator's base must reproduce these or it fails closed; nest-room carves are written in their own section after the base's, and tools/mine_networks_audit.py digests the base section against these figures and checks the replayed volume holds every one

ores.why: vanilla ores the bank buys (data/bank.json: coal, raw copper, raw iron, raw gold, lapis lazuli, redstone, diamond), placed in the exposed walls and roof of the drifts as veins that run back into the rock. `p` is the chance an exposed wall cell seeds a vein; it grows with the level (`depth_gain` per level below the first) and with the walk from the adit (`far_gain`, at 1500 blocks and beyond), and is multiplied in a stope. `y_max`: the highest floor a vein may seed at. Below y0 the deepslate variant is placed; from y0 to y7 a hash chooses.

layer.why: 2026-10-23 (the owner: ore only on the band, more than 1 deep, and some of it hidden): veins grown from the exposed ore into the rock and hidden clusters behind the walls (tools/ore_veins.py), in each tile's own ore function, every line `replace #minecraft:base_stone_overworld`; cover: blocks of ground over every layer cell; every cell stays within 7 (Euclid) of the wall cell it grows from. hidden_rate x a wall's richness (1 + hidden_depth_gain x level) x (1 + hidden_far_gain x far) x (hidden_stope in a stope) is a wall cell's chance of a cluster
